import pandas as pd
t = tables['trips']
t = t[t['fish_date_season']==1]  # season 1 full data only
t['cpa'] = t['yt'] / t['anglers'].replace(0, pd.NA)

# by class
by_cls = t.groupby('cls').agg(trips=('yt','size'), anglers=('anglers','sum'), yt=('yt','sum'))
by_cls['yt_per_angler'] = by_cls['yt']/by_cls['anglers']

# by month bucket (doy//30) and class
t['month_bucket'] = (t['fish_date_doy']//30).astype(int)
by_month = t.groupby('month_bucket').agg(trips=('yt','size'), anglers=('anglers','sum'), yt=('yt','sum'))
by_month['yt_per_angler'] = by_month['yt']/by_month['anglers']

# by month x class (only classes with decent volume)
by_mc = t.groupby(['month_bucket','cls']).agg(trips=('yt','size'), anglers=('anglers','sum'), yt=('yt','sum'))
by_mc['yt_per_angler'] = by_mc['yt']/by_mc['anglers']
by_mc = by_mc[by_mc['trips']>=5].reset_index()

# top boats overall in season with hd_pm / hd_am (common classes)
by_boat = t[t['cls'].isin(['hd_pm','hd_unspecified','hd_am'])].groupby('boat').agg(trips=('yt','size'), anglers=('anglers','sum'), yt=('yt','sum'))
by_boat['yt_per_angler'] = by_boat['yt']/by_boat['anglers']
by_boat = by_boat[by_boat['trips']>=10].sort_values('yt_per_angler', ascending=False).head(15)

result = {
  'by_cls': by_cls.to_dict('index'),
  'by_month': by_month.to_dict('index'),
  'by_mc_top': by_mc.sort_values('yt_per_angler', ascending=False).head(25).to_dict('records'),
  'by_boat_top': by_boat.to_dict('index'),
}

pier['month_bucket'] = (pier['ts_doy']//30).astype(int)

# Season 2, planning turn (day 1) notes

## What season-1 data showed (trips table, season==1, 3650 rows)
- yt-per-angler by class (season total): multi_day 0.73 (NEVER offered to us, ignore),
  day_1_5 0.46, overnight 0.42, three_quarter 0.24, hd_am 0.009, hd_pm 0.010, hd_twilight 0.0,
  full_day: ZERO trips all season (untested/rare - treat as unknown, not proven good or bad).
  => HD_AM / HD_PM / TWILIGHT are basically dead for yellowtail. Don't book them for yt even if
  cheap. (Other agents' baselines B_SAT/B_PERSIST/B_TEMP all live on hd_pm - if their season-2
  numbers stay near ours, that confirms hd_pm is a trap this fishery; watch for it.)
- Seasonality (doy = day of year, doy//30 month buckets): two real windows, not one long summer
  season:
    - SPRING push ~doy 70-140 (roughly Mar-May): day_1_5 ypa 2.2 (n=7, thin), overnight ypa 1.48
      (n=44, solid), three_quarter ypa 0.51 (n=78).
    - FALL push ~doy 250-310 (roughly Sep-Oct): day_1_5 ypa 2.16 (n=69, solid - the single best
      bookable bucket with real volume), overnight ypa 0.69 (n=64), three_quarter ypa 0.30 (n=62).
    - Summer (doy ~150-240, Jun-Aug) was a LULL (ypa 0.02-0.14) despite the warmest pier water of
      the year (peak ~19.3C in month-bucket 5). Water temp alone does NOT predict the bite here -
      don't chase warm water in summer, it was a trap in season 1.
  Caveat: this is one season of data (small n in spots, e.g. spring day_1_5). Treat the fall
  window as higher-confidence than spring. Re-check once season-2 trips start posting.
- Climate at season-2 start: ONI -1.54, PDO -1.57, MEI -2.01 (cool/La Niña-ish). B_TEMP's rule
  (ONI>0) would currently say "don't fish" - worth watching whether that agent sits out and how
  it does; if ONI stays negative most of the year we may want to be more cautious about the
  spring window (cool years can push/delay the yellowtail push).
- PTO arithmetic (from RULES.md, confirmed self-consistent): OVERNIGHT departing Fri or Sat, and
  DAY_1_5 departing Fri, land entirely on the weekend => 0 PTO. That's the free lever - most
  trip volume should come from these, saving the 10 PTO days for weekday trips only when there's
  a live positive signal (fishdope) that fish are actually showing.

## strategy.py (submitted this turn)
Books DAY_1_5 / OVERNIGHT / THREE_QUARTER / FULL_DAY(fallback) only inside the two doy windows
above, skips HD_AM/HD_PM/TWILIGHT entirely, picks the highest-priority affordable in-window
offer each tick. Separately, 14 days ahead of any in-window weekday, commits PTO for it if
pto_left > 2 AND recent fishdope shows yellowtail activity (yt_all/yt_local/wt_all > 0 in last
~6 reports) - so PTO isn't pre-spent on a window that turns out dead. This is a floor/reflex
layer; nightly manual decisions (with full briefing: fleet counts, forecast, actual boat
schedule) should do the sharper boat/day picks and can override/supplement it.

## Budget/PTO pacing plan for nightly self
- Full season budget $2000, PTO 10. Don't blow budget on the spring window alone - fall window
  has the best solid-sample number (day_1_5 ypa 2.16) so keep at least ~$1100-1300 held back for
  Sep-Oct if spring looks marginal.
- Rough allocation target: ~$500-700 spring (mostly overnight, some three_quarter, weekend-
  anchored, 0 PTO), ~$1000-1300 fall (day_1_5 + overnight, weekend-anchored + a few PTO weekdays
  if fishdope confirms), small reserve for late Oct/Nov stragglers.
- Spend PTO conservatively: aim to still have 4-5 PTO left going into the fall window even if
  some got used in spring, since fall is the higher-confidence, higher-yield window.

## What to check next turn / going forward
1. Once season-2 trips start posting, re-run the by-month/by-class query to see if this season's
   timing matches season 1's doy windows (spring ~70-140, fall ~250-310) or has shifted (ONI is
   more negative than probably in season 1 - could delay/shrink the push).
2. Watch leaderboard season_fish once other agents start scoring - that's the real "follow the
   leader" signal (persona instructs following what visibly works, avoiding exact dilution on
   the same boat/class/date). Nobody has a season-2 score yet (day 1).
3. Watch forum for other agents describing what's working; nothing posted yet this season.
4. Re-check fishdope columns (yt_all, yt_local, wt_all) actually populate as expected - only
   inferred meaning from column names, never inspected real fishdope text/values this turn.
5. If season-2 numbers show HD_PM/HD_AM producing real yellowtail (unlike season 1), that's a
   big signal the fishery pattern shifted - revisit the "skip half-days" rule fast.
